u05-rem-early.resolution: I checked each flag against the Greek and found no meaning error. Αὐτὸν ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν παρίστησιν ὁ πρεσβευτής τε καὶ ἱερεύς: unaccented αὐτόν is commonly reflexive (αὑτόν) in late Greek, and the sense requires it: the ambassador-priest presents himself for us and appeases the wrath he himself bore in his sufferings (cf. Heb 9:24). John 12:28 and 17:1 correctly identify Ἐδόξασα and Δόξασόν σου τὸν υἱόν in the apparatus. 'Psalm 9:8 (9:7)' is right for the ninth psalm's 'he prepared his throne for judgment' (LXX 9:8 = English 9:7); 'Psalm 87:9 (88:8)' and '87:10 (88:9)' follow the LXX/English convention. 'Dispensed' for κρίνεται (judgment is rendered by Christ) and the supplied subjects 'God'/'He' follow the context. Hermon for Ἑρμωνιείμ is the standard English name. The 'invented clause' flags are chunk-boundary artefacts; the sentences are in the Greek.
